cases.sentence: Впереди ехал отряд виртембергских гусар, позади, с большою свитой, ехал верхом сам ___.
cases.explain: «Неаполитанский король» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Toward four o’clock in the afternoon Murat’s troops were entering Moscow. In front rode a detachment of Württemberg hussars and behind them rode the King of Naples himself accompanied by a numerous suite.

cases.sentence: Около середины Арбата, близ Николы Явленного, Мюрат остановился, ожидая известия от ___ о том, в каком положении находилась городская крепость «le Kremlin».
cases.explain: «передового отряда» — after the preposition «от», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: About the middle of the Arbát Street, near the Church of the Miraculous Icon of St. Nikoláy, Murat halted to await news from the advanced detachment as to the condition in which they had found the citadel, le Kremlin.

cases.sentence: Вокруг Мюрата собралась ___ людей из остававшихся в Москве жителей.
cases.explain: «небольшая кучка» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Around Murat gathered a group of those who had remained in Moscow. They all stared in timid bewilderment at the strange, long-haired commander dressed up in feathers and gold.

cases.sentence: Все с ___ смотрели на странного, изукрашенного перьями и золотом, длинноволосого начальника.
cases.explain: «робким недоумением» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Around Murat gathered a group of those who had remained in Moscow. They all stared in timid bewilderment at the strange, long-haired commander dressed up in feathers and gold.

cases.explain: «тихие голоса» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Is that their Tsar himself? He’s not bad!” low voices could be heard saying.

cases.sentence: Переводчик обратился к одному ___ и спросил, далеко ли до Кремля?
cases.explain: «старому дворнику» — after the preposition «к», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: “Take off your cap … your caps!” These words went from one to another in the crowd. The interpreter addressed an old porter and asked if it was far to the Krémlin. The porter, listening in perplexity to the unfamiliar Polish accent and not realizing that the interpreter was speaking Russian, did not understand what was being said to him and slipped behind the others.

cases.sentence: Дворник, прислушиваясь с недоумением к чуждому ему ___ и не признавая звуков говора переводчика за русскую речь, не понимал, что̀ ему говорили и прятался за других.
cases.explain: «польскому акценту» — after the preposition «к», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: “Take off your cap … your caps!” These words went from one to another in the crowd. The interpreter addressed an old porter and asked if it was far to the Krémlin. The porter, listening in perplexity to the unfamiliar Polish accent and not realizing that the interpreter was speaking Russian, did not understand what was being said to him and slipped behind the others.

cases.sentence: Один из ___ понял, чего у него спрашивали, и несколько голосов вдруг стали отвечать переводчику.
cases.explain: «русских людей» — after the preposition «из», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Murat approached the interpreter and told him to ask where the Russian army was. One of the Russians understood what was asked and several voices at once began answering the interpreter. A French officer, returning from the advanced detachment, rode up to Murat and reported that the gates of the citadel had been barricaded and that there was probably an ambuscade there.

cases.sentence: Французский офицер из ___ подъехал к Мюрату и доложил, что ворота в крепость заделаны и что вероятно там засада.
cases.explain: «передового отряда» — after the preposition «из», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Murat approached the interpreter and told him to ask where the Russian army was. One of the Russians understood what was asked and several voices at once began answering the interpreter. A French officer, returning from the advanced detachment, rode up to Murat and reported that the gates of the citadel had been barricaded and that there was probably an ambuscade there.

cases.explain: «тесовые щиты» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: The bells in the Krémlin were ringing for vespers, and this sound troubled the French. They imagined it to be a call to arms. A few infantrymen ran to the Kutáfyev Gate. Beams and wooden screens had been put there, and two musket shots rang out from under the gate as soon as an officer and men began to run toward it. A general who was standing by the guns shouted some words of command to the officer, and the latter ran back again with his men.

cases.sentence: Генерал, стоявший у пушек, крикнул офицеру ___, и офицер с солдатами побежал назад.
cases.explain: «командные слова» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
